access_links.label: UNDRR disaster losses and damages tracking system

description: DesInventar Sendai is a network of national disaster loss and damage databases built with the DesInventar methodology and open-source software, promoted by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) for Sendai Framework and Sustainable Development Goal monitoring. National agencies record each disaster event, including small and recurrent local events, at the level of municipalities or districts, with deaths, injured, missing, affected people, destroyed and damaged houses, and damage to infrastructure such as roads, hospitals, schools, crops and livestock, plus economic losses. More than eighty national datasets exist; 65 datasets covering 82 countries and three states were standardised for the 2015 Global Assessment Report. Databases are browsed and queried in the online DesInventar Sendai application and can be exported; the server software itself is open source and free for commercial and non-commercial use under the Apache 2.0 licence, while the data belong to the national custodians. Coverage periods, completeness and update frequency vary by country, many databases are no longer updated, and UNDRR announces a successor disaster losses and damages tracking system. The data support calibration of hazard exposure and loss models, local resilience analysis, emergency response planning and climate adaptation studies, and complement EM-DAT, which captures only large events.
